bug_semantics: An authenticated student who knows an enrolled course ID can request tutor/admin course routes directly. The application treats client-side navigation hiding and Svelte RoleBasedSecurity rendering/redirects as authorization, while route scripts and data services still execute course-ID-keyed reads without enforcing a tutor/admin role at the data boundary. As a result, all-course member profiles, attendance, submissions and answers, marks, and analytics can be returned before the client hides the slot or redirects, producing the advisory's transient sensitive-data disclosure.
flaw_origin: 07eba6b4e0838c8d7d44a133898f8aa4256cdd7b first established the flawed shared authorization mechanism: it added src/components/RoleBasedSecurity/index.svelte, derived the current role from client stores, and rendered its slot only when allowedRoles.includes(userRole); it also hid the Submissions navigation item for role 3 and wrapped admin UI in attendance, people, and submissions routes, but added no server/data-layer role check. Existing route scripts and Supabase services remained reachable and executed independently of that render-only gate, so a crafted course URL bypassed the intended role boundary.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p 07eba6b4e0838c8d7d44a133898f8aa4256cdd7b shows author and committer rotimi-best <best@classroomio.com>, subject 'Limit functionalities by roles', an empty message body, no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, and no bot identity.
evidence: The assigned GitHub advisory and https://github.com/Rivek619/CVE-2025-65670 identify ClassroomIO 0.1.13 and the direct-URL course routes /analytics, /attendance, /submissions, /people, and /marks; the disclosure says a student sees privileged data momentarily before normal restrictions resume.

git show 07eba6b4e0838c8d7d44a133898f8aa4256cdd7b shows one parent, 220f35b3db55f46bc42519b9e82d481c8325a3d6, and a focused authorization change titled 'Limit functionalities by roles'. It creates src/components/RoleBasedSecurity/index.svelte with only a client-store role lookup and {#if allowedRoles.includes(userRole)} slot rendering; it adds role-3 navigation hiding and wraps submissions/admin controls without adding any request-time authorization.

At the BIC, src/utils/services/submissions/index.js fetchSubmissions(course_id) selects submission IDs, question answers, exercise questions/options, status, course, and submitter profile, constrained only by .match({ course_id }); the route's script can invoke this independently of whether RoleBasedSecurity renders its slot. The same commit's attendance and people changes disable or hide controls client-side while their course data remains loaded.

Direct parent-tree verification: git cat-file -e '220f35b3db55f46bc42519b9e82d481c8325a3d6:src/components/RoleBasedSecurity/index.svelte' fails with 'path ... does not exist'; the BIC diff creates that file and introduces the role-based navigation/render checks. Thus the flawed client-only role boundary is absent from the immediate parent.
git tag --contains 07eba6b4e0838c8d7d44a133898f8aa4256cdd7b includes v0.1.0 through the advisory's v0.1.13 and later releases, proving the BIC predates and is contained in the affected release.

The repair is a three-commit linear sequence after v0.2.7: ac4fdf1dd35772a20899e36f5bf55decb1e0ebda migrates client Supabase course, people, submissions, marks, and related reads behind authenticated server endpoints and adds checkUserCoursePermissions; 97d9e490b00f8de355756bd6716d0b607b71712c updates the exercises endpoint and marks page; ac1a05f0068b638e18ed5473fd427506f64a7a1e moves course analytics to /api/courses/analytics and adds an authenticated permission check. git log --reverse v0.2.7..0.2.10 shows exactly that sequence.

Version boundary: git tag --contains ac4fdf1dd35772a20899e36f5bf55decb1e0ebda starts at v0.2.8, while git tag --contains ac1a05f0068b638e18ed5473fd427506f64a7a1e starts at 0.2.10. Therefore ac4fdf1 is the primary direct data-boundary fix and ac1a05f is the terminal fix SHA for the last named analytics route in release 0.2.10.
reasoning: The vulnerability is an authorization-design failure, not merely a visible-navigation bug: course IDs are user-controlled route parameters, and hiding a link or a Svelte slot does not prevent the route script/data request from running. Earlier commits created individual course data reads, but 07eba6b is the smallest causal BIC for this advisory's shared role-bypass mechanism because it is the first commit that declared these functions/routes role-restricted while implementing that restriction solely in the browser across the named admin surfaces. Later Sapper-to-SvelteKit moves, the CourseContainer consolidation, and the May 2024 redirect cleanup preserve or refactor that mechanism and are not BICs. The immediate parent lacks the RoleBasedSecurity component and the newly introduced role-gating changes. The affected v0.1.13 tag contains the BIC. The December 2025 repair moves the sensitive reads to authenticated server endpoints in ac4fdf1, follows with marks/exercises adjustments, and closes the separately named analytics route in ac1a05f at 0.2.10. AI attribution is judged only from the BIC commit object: it has a human author/committer and no AI/bot trailer or marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
